reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid Coinomia Bitcoin-mining contracts, with higher-priced tiers presented as generating more Bitcoin and commissions. It invites participation through signup controls, recruitment and team activity tied to earnings, and links for sharing and joining. The account page does not show submission, payment, actual mining, or realized payouts, and the displayed estimates are not established as guaranteed.

citations.quote: They will then be able to generate bitcoins to you daily.
you will have to recruit more employees... and you will get more money.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker introduces Coinomia as a personal assessment, not a verified return: the description says "in my opinion," and the speaker admits limited familiarity with this kind of investing. The presentation also makes the choice of contract depend on what a viewer can afford. Those qualifications matter. A discussion of a speculative investment can include prices and projected earnings without establishing that the speaker promises any viewer a payout.

citations.quote: in my opinion will be...
I am not too much of this kind of investing but there it is one friend who proposed this plan and that I found very interesting
so it depends on you and the money you have

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's daily-Bitcoin quote describes what the contracts are presented as doing; it does not document a payment, a realized payout, or an unconditional promise. The $10,000 figure identifies a contract price, not proof that anyone bought it. The account form shows an invitation to register, but registration alone does not establish that the speaker concealed investment risk.

citations.quote: They will then be able to generate bitcoins to you daily.
which costs $10,000

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it an opinion does not neutralize the pitch. The speaker presents a $100 entry contract, says mining will produce Bitcoin daily, and describes upgrading to earn more per day. The presentation also directs viewers toward a link. These are concrete inducements to participate, whether or not the recording proves that anyone paid or received a payout.

And they will produce Bitcoins everyday thanks to this option
If you want to upgrade, to make more money per day.
if i offer you you can click on the link at the description

opening.argument: Judge, much of this is a walkthrough of how the proposed business works. The speaker asks what MLM means, explains the role of levels and recruitment, then moves into a calculation example. The displayed calculator separates sales commissions from mining payouts. That combination supports reading the video as an operational demonstration of a proposed model; the figures on a calculator are not evidence that its results were paid out.

citations.quote: if you do not know what MLM-Milcom mix So if you do not know what MLM is It's....
this is an example $100 for each team member

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that recruitment and signup appear, but those details can also be what a walkthrough is explaining. Its account-page observation establishes a displayed form, not a completed registration or purchase. Likewise, the calculator's earnings figure is explicitly presented as an estimate, so it should not be treated as a demonstrated return.

citations.quote: you will have to recruit more employees... and you will get more money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is also a solicitation. The speaker says the launch phase is intended to recruit users, tells viewers they can follow a link, and explains sharing a link so others subscribe. The calculator may be hypothetical, but it illustrates large commission earnings alongside purchasable mining contracts. Teaching the steps does not make the participation pitch incidental.

citations.quote: The administrator of this project gave us this launch stage to recruit as many users as possible
if i offer you you can click on the link at the description
share this link with your other user to see their presence so that they do subscribe

opening.argument: Judge, the visible offer is structured as priced mining contracts with stated mining power and referral commissions. The speaker describes buying a contract and choosing whether to upgrade based on available money. That is consistent with promotion of a paid service with a referral component. The supplied record does not show a completed deposit, functioning mining equipment, or a realized payout, so it cannot establish from those outcomes whether the service delivered or failed to deliver.

citations.quote: You start a 100 $ contract to be an entrepreneur.
so it depends on you and the money you have

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies the strongest concern: daily mining output coupled with earnings from recruitment. But a contract menu and an account form show an offer and a means to join, not whether mining occurs or payments fail. The evidence supports scrutiny of the business claims; it does not independently verify the underlying service's outcome.

citations.quote: They will then be able to generate bitcoins to you daily.
you will have to recruit more employees... and you will get more money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not depend on proving a failed payout. This presentation invites viewers to buy mining contracts, describes Bitcoin output every day, and ties additional money to recruiting people. Its signup and referral path makes the offer actionable. A conventional-looking price menu does not resolve the unsupported mining and earnings claims at the center of the pitch.
